messages.author: c74837073ce57231
messages.subject: Unique Categorical Variables within Surveys
parts:
Hi All,

 

I am relatively new to occupancy modeling and I am currently working on some multi-species occupancy models. I have a question about including categorical explanatory variables for replicates samples/surveys. Apologies in advance if this question is answered somewhere, I have not been able to find an answer yet.


Is it statistically sound to include replicate surveys of a site which all have unique categorical explanatory variables? Each site was surveyed multiple times, but there are no replicates for each categorical variable within each site. See example below.


                                             Categorical Variable

Site 1 –     Survey 1               x1

                Survey 2               x2

                Survey 3               x3


Site 2 –     Survey 1               x1

                Survey 2               x2

                Survey 3               x3


Site 3 –     Survey 1               x1

                Survey 2               x2

   Survey 3               x3


Site 4 –    Survey 1               x1

                Survey 2               x2

   Survey 3               x3

…

 


If so, how does this affect the inferences you are able to make about the effect of this categorical variable, detection and occupancy?

 


Thank you very much,

Bea

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: RE: Unique Categorical Variables within Surveys
parts:
Dear Bea,

I think this is OK, just that you can't separate whatever the levels of that factor are from simple effects of occasion. And we're talking about effects on p, just to be sure, right ? You can't fit any such effects for occupancy, owing to the closure assumption.

Best regards  --  Marc

messages.author: 3dc56a9252202d12
messages.subject: Re: Unique Categorical Variables within Surveys
parts:
Hi Bea, 
Can you clarify a little, are you collecting separate categorical variables in each visit?  Or does the same categorical variable have a different value in each visit?  The former case could be treated as missing data and there are various ways of tackling that problem in estimation.  The latter case may lead to confounding, as Kery mentions.  If you have complete confounding there is no point in trying to estimate an effect for both of the confounded variables, in this case survey visit and variable x.  Just pick 1 and understand that any observed effect could be attributable to either factor.

Cheers,
Dominic

messages.author: c74837073ce57231
messages.subject: Re: Unique Categorical Variables within Surveys
parts:
Thanks for the responses. To clarify, the same categorical variable has a different value in each visit and I am looking at the effects of the categorical variable on p. 

I believe you have answered my question, where the effect of survey visit and variable x are confounded so we couldn't make individual conclusions for each of these variables, but if there was an effect it could be attributable to either variable. 

In reality, the data I'm modelling are more complex than the example I included above. To provide a little more detail, I'm interested in comparing the probabilities of detection between different species groups within each level of variable x. If I have understood correctly, I should be able to make this comparison. Any effects of variable x could also be due to sampling occasion, but the comparisons between species groups would be valid, correct?

Thanks again!
Bea
